name: Eneus Energy Limited
ownership_summary: Incorporated 22 July 2022, registered at Orchard Brae House, 30 Queensferry Road, Edinburgh. Related to Eneus Energy Holdings Limited (SC466495, incorporated 2013, same address; founders Robert Armour and Chris Bronsdon). Carlyle and GIC made a strategic investment in Eneus Energy in 2022, when it was positioned as a green hydrogen/ammonia developer; it has since expanded into data centre development. Which group entity (or SPV) will be the planning applicant is not yet confirmed.

name: Revera Energy
ownership_summary: Carlyle-backed UK energy storage developer named by Eneus as co-developer of the Hunterston data centre; separately developing the consented Hunterston 400 MW/800 MWh BESS (FID June 2026) as part of a 1 GW/2 GWh Scottish portfolio.
notes: The precise contractual split between Eneus and Revera on the data centre is not disclosed.

name: Hunterston Estate (Hunter family)
ownership_summary: The data centre is proposed on Hunterston Estate land in partnership with the estate. Reported context: the estate extends to ~770 acres, ~260 acres owned by the Hunter family with the remainder held by industrial owners after historic compulsory purchase but farmed by the estate.
notes: Land ownership of the specific application parcels not verified against title records.

name: The Carlyle Group
notes: Investor in Eneus Energy (with GIC, since 2022) and backer of Revera Energy.

name: GIC
notes: Singapore sovereign wealth fund; co-investor in Eneus Energy since 2022.

name: Tetra Tech
notes: Environmental/planning consultant; named applicant contact (F.A.O. Stuart Murison) on EIA scoping request 26/00138/EIA.

name: Scottish Water
notes: Developer states Scottish Water has confirmed supply capacity from Camphill Water Treatment Works; scoping consultation response on file.

name: Peel Ports Group (Clydeport)
notes: Owner of the adjacent brownfield Hunterston PARC (former coal terminal) and Hunterston Terminal. No confirmed role in the data centre scheme, which is on Hunterston Estate farmland; included to distinguish the two Hunterston landholdings.

name: Action to Protect Rural Scotland (APRS)
notes: Tracking and opposing the proposal; publicised the 'Defend your Castle' protest at a Clan Hunter gathering.
